description.content: A set of tabs, only one of which is shown at a time.
Distinguishes tabsets from splits.
Uniquely identifies the tabset within the workspace.

Optional in the defaultModel prop and the setModel method; tabsets without ids are assigned ids based on their position (e.g. "tabset-0-1"). Tabsets created by the workspace (e.g. by dropping a tab onto the edge of another tabset) are assigned generated ids.
Size of the tabset within its parent split.

Interpretation rules:

  • Numbers are percentages of the parent split (e.g. size: 25 is 25 percent)
  • Strings may specify other units (e.g. size: "250px"); strings without units are percentages
  • Siblings without a size share the remaining space evenly
String sizes are only initial sizes: they're converted to percentages when the user resizes the split, and (like percentages) they scale with the workspace when it's resized.

A tabset is shown within its minimum and maximum sizes (see minWidth and maxWidth), even if its size is outside of them (e.g. a model saved in a wider window); its size isn't changed, so it's shown at its size again once that fits.
Minimum width of the tabset's content area (not including its header). Overrides the Workspace's tabsetMinWidth prop.

Interpretation rules:

  • Strings must specify a unit: "px", "em", "rem", "vh", or "vw" (e.g. minWidth: "200px")
  • Percentages (and strings without units) are not allowed
Minimum height of the tabset's content area (not including its header). Overrides the Workspace's tabsetMinHeight prop.

Interpretation rules:

  • Strings must specify a unit: "px", "em", "rem", "vh", or "vw" (e.g. minHeight: "200px")
  • Percentages (and strings without units) are not allowed
Maximum width of the tabset's content area (not including its header).

Interpretation rules:

  • Strings must specify a unit: "px", "em", "rem", "vh", or "vw" (e.g. maxWidth: "400px")
  • Percentages (and strings without units) are not allowed
  • If the tabset's minimum width is larger, the minimum is used

A maximum only applies if something else can take up the rest of the space, e.g. another tabset in the same split without a maximum width; otherwise it's ignored (e.g. if every tabset in a split has a maximum, or the tabset fills the workspace).
Maximum height of the tabset's content area (not including its header).

Interpretation rules:

  • Strings must specify a unit: "px", "em", "rem", "vh", or "vw" (e.g. maxHeight: "400px")
  • Percentages (and strings without units) are not allowed
  • If the tabset's minimum height is larger, the minimum is used

A maximum only applies if something else can take up the rest of the space, e.g. another tabset in the same split without a maximum height; otherwise it's ignored (e.g. if every tabset in a split has a maximum, or the tabset fills the workspace).
Where the tabset's tabs are placed relative to its content. Overrides the Workspace's tabPlacement prop.
See the Workspace's tabPlacement prop for how placement affects tabsets.
Tabsets created by the workspace (e.g. by dropping a tab onto the edge of another tabset) use the Workspace's tabPlacement prop.
The tabset isn't removed when its last tab is closed or dragged away; it stays (showing the Workspace's renderEmptyTabset content) until it is closed (see closeTabset).
By default, tabsets without tabs are removed (other than the root tabset of an empty workspace).
Tabsets created by the workspace (e.g. by dropping a tab onto the edge of another tabset) don't keep this flag.
The tabset can be collapsed to just its header (its tab list and toolbar), e.g. a bottom panel or a sidebar.

Tabsets are collapsed by dragging a separator past their minimum size (like collapsible Panels), or with the imperative API (e.g. a button rendered by renderTabsetToolbar, see useParentTabset); clicking a tab (or the empty space in the header) of a collapsed tabset expands it, as does dropping tabs into it from another tabset.
The only tabset in a workspace (the root) can't be collapsed, and neither can a tabset whose siblings are all collapsed.

When tabsets don't fit (e.g. the workspace is made narrower than their minimum sizes), a collapsible tabset may be collapsed to fit. It's shown collapsed (see useParentTabsetState().isCollapsedToFit), but the model isn't changed, so it's shown expanded again once it fits. Until then, it can't be expanded: clicking one of its tabs selects the tab, and expandTabset does nothing. A resize of its split doesn't change it either (it stays expanded in the model, with its size), unless the resize expands it.
Tabsets created by the workspace (e.g. by dropping a tab onto the edge of another tabset) don't keep this flag.
The tabset is collapsed to just its header.
A collapsed tabset's size is the size it expands to; its siblings share the rest of the split.
A collapsed tabset's header runs along its split (e.g. tabs placed on top are shown on the left while a tabset in a horizontal split is collapsed); this doesn't change its tabPlacement.
The user cannot drag the tabset as a whole (by the empty space in its header, or by a TabsetDragHandle).
Its tabs can still be dragged individually (unless they have their own disableDrag flags), and the tabset can still be moved using the imperative API.
Id of the selected tab.

Ids of the tabset's tabs that have been selected, most recently selected first; used to choose which tab to select when the selected tab is removed (see the Workspace's tabRemovalSelectionBehavior prop).
This field is maintained by the workspace, and only when tabRemovalSelectionBehavior is "recent".
Application data for the tabset.
Tabsets created by the workspace start without data.
Tabs in the tabset, in the order they are shown.
